we introduce a novel batch-mode active learning method that is model agnostic and can be used with deep Bayesian active learning methods.

we introduce Information Condensing AL, an AL method that uses the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion to measure the information content of unlabeled points, that we scale our method to the large unlabeled datasets, and that we achieve state-of-the-art accuracy and NLL on several image datasets.

(i) ICAL is an efficient, model agnostic AL method that can be applied to any deep Bayesian model, and (ii) ICAL outperforms state-of-the-art AL methods for Deep Bayesian Learning on image datasets in terms of model performance, and negative log-likelihood.

ICAL is a novel and efficient batch-mode AL algorithm that can improve the performance of deep Bayesian models by focusing the labeling effort on points that contain the most information about the unlabeled data.
ICAL is the state of the art AL method for Deep Bayesian Learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ICAL is the first batch mode active learning method which is model agnostic and works for Deep Bayesian Active Learning.

we have developed a novel method that is capable of learning from a large number of unlabeled data, and is also capable of selecting a subset of this data that can be labeled to maximize the information gain.

ICAL is a batch mode AL method for Deep Bayesian Active Learning which can be used with any deep learning architecture, and it outperforms other state of the art methods on image classification tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ICAL provides a general and effective method to acquire labels for points that are informative in the context of the unlabeled set.
ICAL can be used as a drop in replacement for the standard uncertainty based acquisition functions used for deep learning.
ICAL can be used to improve the performance of Deep Bayesian Active Learning by acquiring informative batches of points.
